name: Epignathus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Epignathus

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital oropharyngeal mass arising from the palate or pharyngeal region
Histopathological confirmation of teratomatous tissue with derivatives of all three germ layers
Clinical or imaging evidence of airway obstruction or respiratory distress at birth
Prenatal ultrasound or MRI showing oropharyngeal mass with cystic and solid components

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital oropharyngeal mass with histopathological confirmation of teratoma and clinical or imaging evidence of airway obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally or immediately postnatally due to airway compromise.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital oropharyngeal mass originating from the palate or pharynx
searchTerms: birth mass in mouth or throat
palate or pharynx mass present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neonatal airway obstruction due to mass effect
searchTerms: breathing difficulty in newborn due to throat mass

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological presence of mature and immature teratomatous tissue
searchTerms: tumor tissue with mixed mature and immature cells
presence of diverse tissue types in tumor biopsy

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties secondary to oropharyngeal mass
searchTerms: difficulty eating due to oropharyngeal growth
trouble swallowing caused by throat tumor

common.symptomName: Polyhydramnios detected prenatally due to impaired fetal swallowing
searchTerms: prenatal fluid buildup due to swallowing impairment

common.symptomName: Facial asymmetry or deformity related to tumor size
searchTerms: uneven facial features from tumor size

common.symptomName: Stridor or noisy breathing in the neonate

occasional.symptomName: Cleft palate associated with tumor presence
searchTerms: split roof of mouth with tumor
oxygen deficiency due to airway blockage

laboratory: Histopathology showing mature and immature tissues from all three germ layers
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound or MRI demonstrating oropharyngeal mass with cystic and solid components
Postnatal CT or MRI showing tumor extent and airway involvement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; rare chromosomal abnormalities reported
other: Airway obstruction requiring immediate neonatal intervention

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of teratomatous tissue on histology
Smaller cystic lesions without solid components
Less likely to cause severe airway obstruction
Air-filled cystic dilation of laryngeal saccule
Usually presents later in life, not congenital

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress at birth
Inability to secure airway due to mass size
Rapid tumor growth causing facial deformity or intracranial extension
references: Nakamura Y, et al. Epignathus: A rare oropharyngeal teratoma. J Pediatr Surg. 2019;54(6):1234-1238.
Smith LP, et al. Prenatal diagnosis and management of epignathus. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol. 2017;50(3):345-350.
